set.seed(1904)
k <- 20; n <- 30; delta <- 0.3

# simulate raw data for one two-group study and keep the summary statistics
sim_study <- function(n, delta) {
  x1 <- rnorm(n, mean = delta, sd = 1)
  x2 <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
  c(m1 = mean(x1), m2 = mean(x2), sd1 = sd(x1), sd2 = sd(x2),
    p = t.test(x1, x2, var.equal = TRUE)$p.value)
}
studies <- as.data.frame(t(replicate(k, sim_study(n, delta))))
studies$n1 <- n; studies$n2 <- n

# vote count

n_sig

# meta-analysis of the same studies (Hedges' g, common-effect model)

code:
set.seed(2019)
nsim <- 4000; n <- 40; m <- 3; rho <- 0.5
se_d <- sqrt(2 / n)
R <- matrix(rho, m, m); diag(R) <- 1
U <- chol(R)

# nsim x nstud x m array of estimated effects under the null
draw <- function(nstud) {
  z <- matrix(rnorm(nsim * nstud * m), ncol = m) %*% U * se_d
  array(z, c(nsim, nstud, m))
}
# two-sided p-value of a common-effect meta-analysis with equal variances
pool_p <- function(est) {
  z <- rowMeans(est) / (se_d / sqrt(ncol(est)))
  2 * pnorm(-abs(z))
}

d5 <- draw(5)
honest <- d5[, , 1]                     # pre-specified outcome
hacked <- apply(d5, c(1, 2), max)       # best of three outcomes
d8 <- draw(8)[, , 1]
dropped <- t(apply(d8, 1, function(x) sort(x, decreasing = TRUE)[1:5]))

fpr <- c(
  study_honest   = mean(2 * pnorm(-abs(honest / se_d)) < 0.05),
  study_hacked   = mean(2 * pnorm(-abs(hacked / se_d)) < 0.05),
  meta_honest    = mean(pool_p(honest) < 0.05),
  meta_hacked    = mean(pool_p(hacked) < 0.05),
  meta_5_of_8    = mean(pool_p(dropped) < 0.05)
)
round(fpr, 3)
#> study_honest study_hacked  meta_honest  meta_hacked  meta_5_of_8 
#>        0.052        0.063        0.050        0.223        0.202

set.seed(303)
M <- 2000; p <- 10
relevant <- rbinom(M, 1, 0.04)
X <- matrix(rnorm(M * p), M, p)
X[relevant == 1, 1:4] <- X[relevant == 1, 1:4] + 1.2   # signal in four features

# initial training set: 2 known relevant and 18 random irrelevant records
screened <- c(sample(which(relevant == 1), 2), sample(which(relevant == 0), 18))
batch <- 20
while (length(screened) < M) {
  train <- data.frame(y = relevant[screened], X[screened, , drop = FALSE])
  model <- suppressWarnings(glm(y ~ ., data = train, family = binomial))
  pool <- setdiff(seq_len(M), screened)
  score <- predict(model, newdata = data.frame(X[pool, , drop = FALSE]))
  screened <- c(screened, pool[order(score, decreasing = TRUE)][seq_len(min(batch, length(pool)))])
}
recall <- cumsum(relevant[screened]) / sum(relevant)

# a naive stopping heuristic: stop after 100 consecutive irrelevant records
run <- 0; stop_at <- NA
for (i in seq_along(screened)) {
  run <- if (relevant[screened[i]] == 1) 0 else run + 1
  if (run >= 100) { stop_at <- i; break }
}
c(total_relevant = sum(relevant),
  screened_for_95pct_recall = which(recall >= 0.95)[1],
  screened_for_100pct_recall = which(recall >= 1)[1],
  heuristic_stop = stop_at,
  recall_at_stop = round(recall[stop_at], 3))
#>             total_relevant  screened_for_95pct_recall 
#>                     85.000                    667.000 
#> screened_for_100pct_recall             heuristic_stop 
#>                   1607.000                    621.000 
#>             recall_at_stop 
#>                      0.941
curve_df <- data.frame(screened = seq_along(recall), recall = recall)
ggplot(curve_df, aes(screened, recall)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1 / M, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = stop_at, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, colour = "grey50") +
  labs(x = "Records screened", y = "Recall")

compare_extractions <- function(a, b, id = "study_id") {

heading: 4.1 Inverse-variance weighting
text:
Suppose \(k\) studies estimate quantity \(\theta\) independent, unbiased estimates \(y_i\) whose variances \(v_i\) known. Among weighted averages \(\sum_i w_i y_i / \sum_i w_i\), one smallest variance uses weights proportional inverse variances, \(w_i = 1/v_i\):\[
\hat\theta = \frac{\sum_{=1}^k w_i y_i}{\sum_{=1}^k w_i}, \qquad
\operatorname{Var}(\hat\theta) = \frac{1}{\sum_{=1}^k w_i}, \qquad w_i = \frac{1}{v_i}.
\]standard result combining independent estimates reason inverse-variance weighting underlies almost every meta-analytic model. Two features deserve emphasis. First, variance pooled estimate reciprocal total weight: information adds across studies. Second, derivation treats \(v_i\) known constants. practice estimates, effect sizes (SMDs, log odds ratios) depend \(y_i\) , introduces small biases weights. models inherit assumption; usually harmless studies small.Throughout chapter use BCG vaccine trials (Colditz et al. 1994), log risk ratio tuberculosis vaccinated versus unvaccinated participants effect size. ci_dl <- function(yi, vi, level = 0.95) {
  k <- length(yi); w <- 1 / vi
  Q <- sum(w * (yi - sum(w * yi) / sum(w))^2)
  tau2 <- max(0, (Q - (k - 1)) / (sum(w) - sum(w^2) / sum(w)))
  ws <- 1 / (vi + tau2)
  mu <- sum(ws * yi) / sum(ws)
  q  <- sum(ws * (yi - mu)^2) / (k - 1)
  se_w <- sqrt(1 / sum(ws))
  se_h <- sqrt(q / sum(ws))
  se_a <- sqrt(max(1, q) / sum(ws))
  zc <- qnorm(1 - (1 - level) / 2); tc <- qt(1 - (1 - level) / 2, k - 1)
  c(wald_lb = mu - zc * se_w, wald_ub = mu + zc * se_w,
    hksj_lb = mu - tc * se_h, hksj_ub = mu + tc * se_h,
    adhoc_lb = mu - tc * se_a, adhoc_ub = mu + tc * se_a)
}
chk <- ci_dl(dat$yi, dat$vi)
rbind(by_hand = chk[c("wald_lb", "wald_ub", "hksj_lb", "hksj_ub")],
      rma = c(unlist(rma(yi, vi, data = dat, method = "DL")[c("ci.lb", "ci.ub")]),
              unlist(rma(yi, vi, data = dat, method = "DL", test = "knha")[c("ci.lb", "ci.ub")])))
#>         wald_lb wald_ub hksj_lb hksj_ub
#> by_hand  -1.064 -0.3638  -1.108 -0.3204
#> rma      -1.064 -0.3638  -1.108 -0.3204
set.seed(4)
sim_coverage <- function(k, tau2, nrep = 1000, mu = 0.3) {
  hits <- replicate(nrep, {
    ni <- sample(20:200, k, replace = TRUE)
    vi <- 4 / ni
    yi <- rnorm(k, mu, sqrt(tau2 + vi))
    ci <- ci_dl(yi, vi)
    c(Wald = ci[["wald_lb"]] <= mu & mu <= ci[["wald_ub"]],
      HKSJ = ci[["hksj_lb"]] <= mu & mu <= ci[["hksj_ub"]],
      adhoc = ci[["adhoc_lb"]] <= mu & mu <= ci[["adhoc_ub"]])
  })
  rowMeans(hits)
}
grid <- expand.grid(k = c(5, 10), tau2 = c(0, 0.05, 0.2))
cov_res <- cbind(grid, t(mapply(sim_coverage, grid$k, grid$tau2)))
cov_res
#>    k tau2  Wald  HKSJ adhoc
#> 1  5 0.00 0.962 0.944 0.996
#> 2 10 0.00 0.964 0.949 0.987
#> 3  5 0.05 0.900 0.948 0.972
#> 4 10 0.05 0.929 0.959 0.968
#> 5  5 0.20 0.884 0.953 0.965
#> 6 10 0.20 0.929 0.955 0.961
cov_long <- reshape(cov_res, direction = "long",
                    varying = c("Wald", "HKSJ", "adhoc"), v.names = "coverage",
                    timevar = "method", times = c("Wald", "HKSJ", "adhoc"))
ggplot(cov_long, aes(factor(tau2), coverage, colour = method, group = method)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.95, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~ k, labeller = label_both) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.8, 1)) +
  labs(x = expression(tau^2), y = "Coverage of 95% CI", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

text:

\[
y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_{i1} + \dots + \beta_{p'} x_{ip'} + u_i + \varepsilon_i, \qquad u_i \sim N(0, \tau^2_{\text{res}}), \qquad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0, v_i).

\]

text:

Johnson–Neyman technique instead finds every value \(w\) \(\hat\psi(w)\) exactly boundary significance (Bauer Curran 2005). Setting \(\hat\psi(w)^2 = c^2\, \mathrm{Var}\{\hat\psi(w)\}\), \(c\) critical value reference distribution (\(z\) \(t\)), gives quadratic

\]

heading: 5.4.1 Implementation
text: three functions work rma.uni rma.mv fit two-way interaction continuous moderators. take coefficients covariance matrix fitted model, use reference distribution model (normal test = "z", \(t\) model’s degrees freedom test = "knha" test = "t"), check moderator binary, classify region according sign \(\) rather testing random point.
code:
jn_parts <- function(fit, pred, mod, level = 0.95) {
  b <- coef(fit)
  if (!pred %in% names(b)) stop("'", pred, "' is not a model coefficient.")
  int <- intersect(c(paste0(pred, ":", mod), paste0(mod, ":", pred)), names(b))
  if (length(int) != 1) stop("No ", pred, " x ", mod, " interaction in the model.")
  if (length(unique(fit$X[, mod])) <= 2)
    stop("'", mod, "' is binary: the Johnson-Neyman technique needs a continuous moderator.")
  V <- vcov(fit)
  ddf <- fit$ddf
  df <- if (length(ddf) > 1) ddf[[match(pred, names(b))]] else ddf[[1]]
  crit <- if (is.null(df) || is.na(df)) qnorm(1 - (1 - level) / 2) else
    qt(1 - (1 - level) / 2, df)
  list(b1 = b[[pred]], b3 = b[[int]], v11 = V[pred, pred], v33 = V[int, int],
       v13 = V[pred, int], crit = crit, df = df, w = fit$X[, mod])
}

jn_slopes <- function(fit, pred, mod, at, level = 0.95) {
  p <- jn_parts(fit, pred, mod, level)
  est <- p$b1 + p$b3 * at
  se <- sqrt(p$v11 + 2 * at * p$v13 + at^2 * p$v33)
  stat <- est / se
  pval <- if (is.null(p$df) || is.na(p$df)) 2 * pnorm(-abs(stat)) else 2 * pt(-abs(stat), p$df)
  data.frame(at = at, estimate = est, se = se,
             ci.lb = est - p$crit * se, ci.ub = est + p$crit * se, pval = pval)
}

jn_region <- function(fit, pred, mod, level = 0.95) {
  p <- jn_parts(fit, pred, mod, level)
  A <- p$b3^2 - p$crit^2 * p$v33
  B <- 2 * (p$b1 * p$b3 - p$crit^2 * p$v13)
  C <- p$b1^2 - p$crit^2 * p$v11
  disc <- B^2 - 4 * A * C
  if (A == 0) {
    bounds <- -C / B
    where <- if (B > 0) "above the bound" else "below the bound"
  } else if (disc < 0) {
    bounds <- numeric(0)
    where <- if (A > 0) "everywhere" else "nowhere"
  } else {
    bounds <- sort((-B + c(-1, 1) * sqrt(disc)) / (2 * A))
    where <- if (A > 0) "outside the bounds" else "between the bounds"
  }
  list(bounds = bounds, significant = where, observed = range(p$w),
       crit = p$crit, df = p$df)
}

jn_plot <- function(fit, pred, mod, level = 0.95, shift = 0, n = 200,
                    xlab = mod, ylab = paste("Conditional effect of", pred)) {
  p <- jn_parts(fit, pred, mod, level)
  grid <- seq(min(p$w), max(p$w), length.out = n)
  d <- jn_slopes(fit, pred, mod, at = grid, level = level)
  d$sig <- d$pval < 1 - level
  reg <- jn_region(fit, pred, mod, level)
  vb <- reg$bounds[reg$bounds >= min(p$w) & reg$bounds <= max(p$w)]
  ggplot(d, aes(x = at + shift, y = estimate)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci.lb, ymax = ci.ub), fill = "grey80") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
    geom_line(aes(colour = sig, group = 1), linewidth = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = vb + shift, linetype = 3) +
    geom_rug(data = data.frame(w = p$w), aes(x = w + shift), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey40", `TRUE` = "firebrick"),
                        labels = c(`FALSE` = "not significant", `TRUE` = "significant"),
                        name = NULL) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

set.seed(2026)
arms <- list(control = rnorm(40, 50, 10), low = rnorm(40, 45, 10), high = rnorm(40, 42, 10))
s <- data.frame(arm = names(arms), n = lengths(arms),
                m = sapply(arms, mean), sd = sapply(arms, sd))
s
#>             arm  n     m     sd
#> control control 40 49.59  9.991
#> low         low 40 43.70  9.052
#> high       high 40 40.60 11.542
combine_groups <- function(n1, m1, s1, n2, m2, s2) {
  n <- n1 + n2
  m <- (n1 * m1 + n2 * m2) / n
  sd <- sqrt(((n1 - 1) * s1^2 + (n2 - 1) * s2^2 + n1 * n2 / n * (m1 - m2)^2) / (n - 1))
  c(n = n, m = m, sd = sd)
}
ctl <- s[s$arm == "control", ]; low <- s[s$arm == "low", ]; high <- s[s$arm == "high", ]

# (1) naive: both comparisons, control counted twice
naive <- escalc("MD", m1i = c(low$m, high$m), sd1i = c(low$sd, high$sd), n1i = c(40, 40),
                m2i = rep(ctl$m, 2), sd2i = rep(ctl$sd, 2), n2i = c(40, 40))
# (2) split the control group
split <- escalc("MD", m1i = c(low$m, high$m), sd1i = c(low$sd, high$sd), n1i = c(40, 40),
                m2i = rep(ctl$m, 2), sd2i = rep(ctl$sd, 2), n2i = c(20, 20))
# (3) combine the two active arms
cg <- combine_groups(40, low$m, low$sd, 40, high$m, high$sd)
comb <- escalc("MD", m1i = cg["m"], sd1i = cg["sd"], n1i = cg["n"],
               m2i = ctl$m, sd2i = ctl$sd, n2i = 40)
# (4) keep both, with the exact covariance from the shared control
V <- diag(naive$vi)
V[1, 2] <- V[2, 1] <- ctl$sd^2 / 40
fix_rows <- rbind(
  naive    = unlist(rma(yi, vi, data = naive, method = "EE")[c("beta", "se")]),
  split    = unlist(rma(yi, vi, data = split, method = "EE")[c("beta", "se")]),
  combined = c(comb$yi, sqrt(comb$vi)),
  gls      = unlist(rma.mv(naive$yi, V)[c("beta", "se")]))
colnames(fix_rows) <- c("estimate", "se")
round(fix_rows, 3)

heading: 6.3.1 Model and interpretation
text:
three-level model represents hierarchical dependence directly (Konstantopoulos 2011; Cheung 2014; Van den Noortgate et al. 2012):
\[
y_{ij} = \mu + u_{(3)j} + u_{(2)ij} + \varepsilon_{ij}, \qquad u_{(3)j} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_{(3)}), \quad u_{(2)ij} \sim N(0, \sigma^2_{(2)}), \quad \varepsilon_{ij} \sim N(0, v_{ij}).
\]
Level 1 sampling error, level 2 variation among effects within clusters, level 3 variation clusters. total heterogeneity \(\sigma^2_{(2)} + \sigma^2_{(3)}\), two effects cluster covariance \(\sigma^2_{(3)}\), intra-cluster correlation true effects \(\sigma^2_{(3)} / (\sigma^2_{(2)} + \sigma^2_{(3)})\). model assumes sampling errors independent, exactly right independent samples nested clusters approximation effects share participants. metafor rma.mv() random = ~ 1 | cluster/effect.

i2_levels <- function(fit) {
  w <- 1 / fit$vi
  k <- fit$k
  vtyp <- (k - 1) * sum(w) / (sum(w)^2 - sum(w^2))
  s2 <- fit$sigma2
  out <- 100 * c(s2, vtyp) / (sum(s2) + vtyp)
  names(out) <- c(paste0("level", length(s2) + 2 - seq_along(s2)), "level1 (sampling)")
  round(out, 1)
}

# intercept, SE, and one-sided p-value for H0: beta0 <= 0
icpt <- function(fit) {
  if (inherits(fit, "rma")) {
    est <- coef(fit)[1]; se <- fit$se[1]; p1 <- pnorm(est / se, lower.tail = FALSE)
  } else {
    cf <- summary(fit)$coefficients
    est <- cf[1, 1]; se <- cf[1, 2]
    p1 <- pt(est / se, df = fit$df.residual, lower.tail = FALSE)
  }
  c(estimate = unname(est), se = unname(se), p_one_sided = unname(p1))
}

pet_peese <- function(pet, peese, alpha = 0.05) {
  use_peese <- icpt(pet)["p_one_sided"] < alpha
  out <- if (use_peese) icpt(peese) else icpt(pet)
  data.frame(selected = if (use_peese) "PEESE" else "PET",
             estimate = round(out[["estimate"]], 3), se = round(out[["se"]], 3))
}

  keep <- p < alpha & z > 0                    # significant, in the expected direction
  z <- z[keep]; p <- p[keep]
  z_full <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)               # critical z for p < .05
  z_half <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 4)               # critical z for p < .025
  half <- p < alpha / 2
  # noncentrality that gives 33% power for a two-sided z-test at level alpha
  ncp33 <- uniroot(function(m) pnorm(z_full - m, lower.tail = FALSE) - 1/3,
                   c(0, 10))$root
  stouffer <- function(pp) {
    pp <- pmin(pmax(pp, 1e-10), 1 - 1e-10)
    Z <- sum(qnorm(pp)) / sqrt(length(pp))
    c(Z = Z, p = pnorm(Z))
  }
  # right skew: pp-values under the null of no effect
  pp0_full <- p / alpha
  pp0_half <- p[half] / (alpha / 2)
  # flatness: P(result at least as weak as observed | significant, 33% power)
  pow_half <- pnorm(z_half - ncp33, lower.tail = FALSE)
  pp33_full <- (pnorm(z - ncp33) - pnorm(z_full - ncp33)) / (1 / 3)
  pp33_half <- (pnorm(z[half] - ncp33) - pnorm(z_half - ncp33)) / pow_half
  out <- rbind("Right skew, full curve"      = stouffer(pp0_full),
               "Right skew, half curve"      = stouffer(pp0_half),
               "Flatter than 33%, full curve" = stouffer(pp33_full),
               "Flatter than 33%, half curve" = stouffer(pp33_half))
  attr(out, "k") <- c(significant = length(p), below_025 = sum(half))
  out
}

fit_spec <- function(metric, method, test, trials) {

Let \(y_i\) estimate study \(= 1, \ldots, k\) known standard error \(\sigma_i\). 
normal-normal hierarchical model (NNHM) 
\[
\begin{aligned}
y_i \mid \theta_i &\sim N(\theta_i, \sigma_i^2), \\
\theta_i \mid \mu, \tau &\sim N(\mu, \tau^2), \\
(\mu, \tau) &\sim p(\mu)\, p(\tau).
\end{aligned}
\]
first two lines random-effects model; third adds priors, usually independent,

\frac{1}{\sqrt{\sigma_i^2 + \tau^2}}\,
\phi\!\left(\frac{y_i - \mu}{\sqrt{\sigma_i^2 + \tau^2}}\right).

pw_df <- as.data.frame(pw)
# orient every contrast as "treat2 versus treat1" with treat1 = No contact
get_direct <- function(trt) {
  d <- subset(pw_df, (treat1 == "No contact" & treat2 == trt) |
                     (treat2 == "No contact" & treat1 == trt))
  yi <- ifelse(d$treat1 == "No contact", -d$TE, d$TE)  # log OR trt vs No contact

}
ind_vs_nc <- get_direct("Individual")

    treat * (theta + u_k[k] + gamma_w * (age - 60)) + rnorm(n_k[k], 0, 12)
  data.frame(trial = k, age = age, treat = treat, sbp = sbp)
}))

}))

  if (lb < 1 && ub > 1) return(-1)
  if (N < ois_n) return(-1)
  0
}

grade_label <- function(s) {

per1000 <- function(x) round(1000 * x)
diff_text <- function(acr, rr, lb, ub) {
  d <- per1000(acr * (c(rr, lb, ub) - 1))
  dir <- function(v) if (v < 0) paste(abs(v), "fewer") else paste(v, "more")
  sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", dir(d[1]), dir(d[2]), dir(d[3]))
}

heading: 16.5 Reporting checklist
text:
Whatever method, report let reader reproduce analysis judge certainty
conclusions (Chapter 15). minimum states registered protocol
deviations; presents PRISMA 2020 flow diagram; tabulates study characteristics 
risk--bias ratings; names effect-size metric, model, heterogeneity estimator, 
confidence-interval method; reports pooled estimate confidence interval, tau, 
prediction interval; describes moderator, sensitivity, publication-bias analyses,
including change conclusion; rates certainty GRADE; shares 
extracted data analysis code.
